Label the \(3\times 3\) points as
\[
\begin{matrix}
A&B&C\\
D&E&F\\
G&H&I
\end{matrix}
\]
where \(E\) is the center.

The only lines containing three of the points are:
- the three rows \(ABC,DEF,GHI\);
- the three columns \(ADG,BEH,CFI\);
- the two diagonals \(AEI,CEG\).

First, fewer than \(3\) removals cannot work:

- If the center \(E\) is not removed, then each of the four lines through \(E\), namely \(DEF,BEH,AEI,CEG\), must have a point removed. Apart from \(E\), every point lies on at most one of these four lines, so two removals could destroy at most two of them. Impossible.
- Thus \(E\) must be removed. If only one more point were removed, that single point would have to break all four outer side lines \(ABC,GHI,ADG,CFI\). But any point lies on at most two of these, which is not enough.

So at least \(3\) removals are needed.

Three removals are enough: remove \(A,E,I\). Then every possible three-point line contains at least one removed point.

\[
